proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1205, what is the maximum rise of a stair flight between landings, the maximum riser height, and the minimum tread depth?

options.text: Maximum rise 3.00 m; maximum riser 175 mm; minimum tread 280 mm
Maximum rise 3.60 m; maximum riser 200 mm; minimum tread 250 mm
Maximum rise 4.20 m; maximum riser 200 mm; minimum tread 300 mm
Maximum rise 3.60 m; maximum riser 250 mm; minimum tread 200 mm

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1205 sets: maximum rise between landings = 3.60 m; maximum individual riser height = 200 mm; minimum tread depth = 250 mm. Exceeding 3.60 m between landings creates fatigue and disorientation during emergency egress. The 200 mm riser and 250 mm tread are the dimensional limits that define a safely climbable stair.
proposed.explanation: The three stair dimension values (3.60 m between landings, 200 mm riser max, 250 mm tread min) are frequently tested together as a set. Confusing riser and tread values (swapping 200/250) is the most common error.
